angle: Low-normal ferritin and inflammation-masked ferritin; what to ask for
hook: Your report says your ferritin is normal. You're still exhausted, and nobody can tell you why.
draft:
Your ferritin is "normal". You're still exhausted. Both can be true.

Think of haemoglobin as the money in your wallet and ferritin as your savings. You can have enough in the wallet, so no anaemia, while the savings are almost empty.

Most lab reports flag ferritin only when it's very low. A low-normal number rarely gets a second look.

There's a well-known trial on exactly this. In 2012, researchers gave 198 menstruating women with unexplained fatigue either iron or a placebo for 12 weeks. None of them were anaemic. All had ferritin under 50. Fatigue scores dropped 47.7% with iron and 28.8% with the placebo.

There's a second catch. Ferritin rises when there's inflammation in the body, even if your iron stores are low. That's why WHO guidance says that in adults with infection or inflammation, a ferritin below 70 may still point to iron deficiency.

What I look at with clients:

- Ferritin with a CRP, never alone.
- Where the iron is going: heavy periods, or a gut that isn't absorbing it.
- If you take thyroid medication, iron timing. The two compete, so ask your doctor how far apart to take them.

If you're tired and your report says normal, ask for the actual ferritin number and a CRP. Then take both to your doctor.

#IronDeficiency #WomensHealth
final:
Your report says your ferritin is normal. You're still exhausted, and nobody can tell you why.

Think of haemoglobin as the cash in your wallet and ferritin as your savings. Your wallet can be fine, so you're not anaemic, while your savings are nearly gone.

Most reports only flag ferritin when it's very low, so a low-normal number rarely gets a second look.

A 2012 trial in the Canadian Medical Association Journal tested what happens next. It gave 198 menstruating women with unexplained fatigue either iron or a placebo for 12 weeks. None were anaemic, and all had ferritin under 50. Fatigue scores fell 47.7% with iron and 28.8% with the placebo.

Inflammation muddies the number further. Ferritin goes up when the body is inflamed, even if iron stores are low. WHO guidance says that in adults with infection or inflammation, a ferritin below 70 may still point to iron deficiency.

So with my clients I check:

- Ferritin alongside CRP, not on its own.
- Where the iron is going: heavy periods, or a gut that isn't absorbing it.
- Iron timing for anyone on thyroid medication, because the two interfere with each other. Your doctor can tell you how far apart to take them.

If you're tired and your report says normal, ask for the actual ferritin value and a CRP, and take both to your doctor.

#IronDeficiency #WomensHealth

sources.title: Vaucher P et al. Effect of iron supplementation on fatigue in nonanemic menstruating women with low ferritin: RCT. CMAJ 2012;184(11):1247-54
sources.claim: 198 women, ferritin <50, Hb >12; fatigue -47.7% iron vs -28.8% placebo over 12 weeks

sources.title: WHO guideline on use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations (2020)

claims_checked.claim: Trial was industry-funded (Pierre Fabre); effect on fatigue only, not quality of life
